items.title: Buzzy Williams Interview, 1980-06-18
items.q: We had another fellow working behind a boy named Bobby Lay, who was an old entertainer from around California.

ctx.x: The Court Tavern. The Court Tavern, that's right.

Yeah, that's right. He built a tavern for me and him. Yeah. That's right. He built a piano, what they call a gay nineties in there. Uh-huh. Him and I was raised, we had blazers and I had a straw hat and I raised a mustache. We had another fellow working behind a boy named Bobby Lay, who was an old entertainer from around California. She paints her cheeks like roses She paints her way dear smile She colours up She paints them black or brown. She paints her lips rosy red, puts on a silken gown, and every night you'll find her painting New Yorktown. You see, after 1915, people used to frown on people using paint. I remember when I first came here, I could still see them. People would be sitting on the front porch and taking red brick, shacking it down. I'm talking about people in town.
